title: Establish PRD Sign-off Playbook & Cross-Team Dependency Checklist for Model Serving Rollouts
creator: Ava Thompson
description:
Problem: Multiple past PRDs for serving rollouts (new model variants, quantization profiles, and routing policies) have encountered delays during handoff because acceptance criteria were underspecified for Design, Legal, and Security. This ticket defines a lightweight, repeatable playbook and dependency checklist to ensure timely cross-team reviews and clear sign-off criteria for model serving rollouts.

Scope: produce a PRD sign-off template, per-team checklists (Engineering, Design, Legal, Security, SRE), a gating matrix with required artifacts, and an operational runbook for sign-off timelines and escalation. Excludes implementation of rollout automation and any policy changes to enterprise contracts; those will be separate follow-ups.

Goal: reduce sign-off cycle time to <= 10 business days for routine rollouts and surface any hard blockers within 48 hours of PRD circulation.
summary_of_discussions: 2025-02-12: Kickoff with ENG/Design/Legal/Security to align on problem statement and success metrics.

2025-02-19: Engineering proposed a minimal acceptance criteria set that covers performance regression thresholds and fallback behavior; Design requested clarified UX acceptance for streaming and tool-calling flows.
2025-02-25: Legal flagged three contract-level items that require templated language for customer-facing changelogs and data-processing notes.
2025-03-03: Security requested an itemized list for KMS/HSM dependencies and an audit log sampling plan; agreed to include as checklist items rather than gate the initial sign-off.
2025-03-04: Decided to pilot the playbook on the next model catalog rollout (model-mosaic v2) with a retro after sign-off to iterate on templates.
decisions: Adopt a single PRD sign-off template used by PMs and required for any rollout touching runtime or private deployments.
Use a three-tier gate: Review (informational), Conditional Sign-off (requires fixes but not blocking), Final Sign-off (go/no-go).
Acceptance criteria will be Boolean checklist items where possible and include quantitative thresholds for latency/cost/regression where applicable.
open_questions: What is the maximum set of legal language we can standardize vs. when legal must craft bespoke clauses (list examples to scope).
Should Design sign-off require a production demo for streaming UX changes or is a prototype video sufficient for low-risk changes?
Do we require a dedicated SRE runbook entry for every model variant rollout or only for changes to autoscaling/config?
acceptance_criteria: A single PRD sign-off template is created and stored in Confluence with placeholders for artifacts and timelines.
Per-team checklists (Engineering, Design, Legal, Security, SRE) are written, reviewed, and each has a named reviewer for the pilot rollout.
A gating matrix describing Review / Conditional / Final sign-off states and the artifacts required for each state is published.
Pilot the playbook on the model-mosaic v2 rollout and collect time-to-sign-off and blockers for a retro.
At least one legal template for customer-facing changelog language and one data-processing blurb are approved by Legal.
tasks: PM: Draft the PRD sign-off template and example completed template for model-mosaic v2 (Ava).
ENG: Produce performance test checklist and define regression thresholds for latency and token cost (refer ENG-2012).
DES: Produce UX acceptance checklist for streaming and tool-calling flows and record a demo clip for the pilot (refer DES-145).
LEGAL: Author two template blurbs (changelog + data processing) and confirm when bespoke language is needed (refer SEC-87 for overlap).
SEC: Provide required KMS/HSM checklist items and audit log sampling expectations.
PM: Run pilot sign-off and schedule retro within 5 business days after sign-off.
signoff_status: Engineering provisional sign-off obtained 2025-03-01; Design and Legal pending; Security provided conditional checklist items.
notes: Pilot chosen to be lightweight: for the pilot, conditional sign-offs can be continued post-release if issues are low-risk and tracked in follow-up tickets. PM to escalate any Legal blockers to GC by 2025-03-10 if not resolved. Expect iteration after pilot retro.
